newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end mixed as liquidity tightens.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end mixed as liquidity tightens.

text.p: Taiwan share prices wobbled to a mixed close on Friday on caution that analysts attributed to the central bank's latest drive to tighten money market liquidity.
The bank acted on Thursday to push the overnight interbank rate to 7.001 percent at Thursday's close, a recent high.
The index opened higher, then dipped for much of the session before closing a scant 8.96 points or 0.10 percent higher at 8,593.08. Turnover was a hectic T$174 billion.
Brokers said the mixed trading also reflected lingering worries over the central bank's Wednesday call for extra caution in the red-hot stock market, which sparked a fall on Thursday.
Rumours had swirled on Thursday that the central bank might raise the rediscount rate, allowing the market to breath a sigh of relief when no change was announced, brokers said.
"In the end it wasn't true and that's why the index today opened higher," said National Securities analyst Alex Yang.
Golden Securities research chief Albert Lin said: "The lack of a rate hike reaffirmed market expectations that the central bank would not take any drastic moves to hit the market."
Electronics rose 3.50 percent, led by Taiwan Semiconductor, which surged the daily seven percent limit to T$85 on word that it planned a new T$400 billion microchip project.
Electricals, chemicals, steels, and plastics rose.

But financials tumbled 2.51 percent as investors defied analysts' expectations that Thursday's dividend issues by the Big Three state banks -- Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan -- would trigger a further rally.
After rising on Thursday, Chang Hwa fell T$6.5 to T$118.5, First T$6 to T$120.5 and Hua Nan T$6.5 to T$108.5.

Brokers said the central bank's repeated issuance of negotiable certificates of deposit to soak up loose liquidity -- it issued T$3 billion in NCDs on Thursday -- was likely to keep stock investors wary in the short run.
